indicators.note: something done unusually is done out of its normal order, so the shortened word's letters are rearranged
abridged means shortened, so the word piece loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A literary extract has been cut down in an odd way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abridged' cuts PIECE to PIEC, and 'Unusually' rearranges those letters; the whole clue doubles as the definition, since a long poem is a piece of literature.
explanation.definitionFit: A long narrative poem of heroic deeds is a classic form of literary work.

indicators.note: one thing found in another sits inside it, so the word for anything goes within the doctors' letters

parts.note: DR is the standard abbreviation for doctor, so doctors gives DRS
aught is an old word meaning anything at all

explanation.surface: Whatever is in the medicine a doctor prescribes.
explanation.definitionFit: A draught is a measured drink of medicine, so the plural means doses taken by mouth.

clue.text: Crew said it's likely to be passed at Chiswick

definitions.text: it's likely to be passed at Chiswick

indicators.note: said signals that the word for a crew is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a rowing crew in a racing boat is an eight

explanation.surface: A rowing crew is told what it will pass during a race at Chiswick.
explanation.walkthrough: An eyot (pronounced like 'eight') is a small river island; Chiswick Eyot on the Thames is passed in the Oxford and Cambridge Boat Race, a famous annual rowing race in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Chiswick Eyot is a small island in the Thames that rowers pass on the Boat Race course.

parts.note: pre- is the prefix meaning before
Sir Walter Scott, the Scottish novelist

explanation.surface: A man called John comes ahead of one called Walter.
explanation.walkthrough: John Prescott was a British Labour politician and Deputy Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: John Prescott was Tony Blair's Deputy Prime Minister, so his first name serves as the definition.

parts.note: in the fairy tale the ugly duckling turns out to be a young swan, so the clue asks for the proper term for a baby swan

explanation.definitionFit: In Andersen's tale the so-called ugly duckling is really a baby swan, which has its own name.

clue.text: Winter coat could be additional to shorts

indicators.note: could be says the letters of the words before it may become something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A winter coat might be worn over a pair of shorts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shorts' are not trousers but small measures of spirits, such as gin, to which this mixer is added.
explanation.definitionFit: This fizzy quinine mixer is commonly added to a short such as gin.

clue.text: The same set-up applied to company doctor

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means written upwards, so the Latin word is read backwards

parts.note: idem is Latin for the same

explanation.surface: An identical arrangement is used by a firm's doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Medico is a jocular or informal word for a doctor or medical student.

clue.text: Editorial self-reference by newsman is not new …

parts.note: a newspaper editorial refers to itself as we, and us is the object form
ED is short for editor, a newsman in charge of a paper

explanation.surface: A journalist refers to himself in the editorial voice, and it is old news.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs this clue on into 13-down.
explanation.definitionFit: Something used has been owned before, so it is second-hand rather than brand new.

definitions.meaning: ... as an adjective means plump or overweight
here used loosely for something misleading

explanation.definitionFit: The word means plump, and in British rhyming slang (porky pie, lie) it means a fib that misleads.

parts.note: Trigger was the name of a famous screen cowboy's horse, so a cowboy happy with Trigger is that horse's rider

explanation.definitionFit: The singing cowboy star of Western films rode a palomino horse called Trigger.

clue.text: Politeness not unknown to an intriguing lady

indicators.note: not says the following letter for an unknown is left out of the word

parts.note: courtesy means politeness
Y is a mathematical unknown, like x

explanation.surface: A scheming woman is anything but polite to an outsider.
explanation.definitionFit: A courtesan was a mistress to wealthy men, often involved in court intrigue.

parts.note: the numeral 1 is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: off says the letters of laid go wrong and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A number is put out of play within a number.
explanation.walkthrough: The final '1' points to 1-down, whose answer means a long heroic poem, which this is.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's poem about the Trojan War is the archetypal epic, the answer to 1-down.

clue.text: Turn to welcome a tragic visitor to Cyprus

indicators.note: turn tells us to read the next small word backwards

parts.note: hello is a word of welcome

explanation.surface: Greeting a doomed traveller arriving on Cyprus.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's tragic Moor is sent to Cyprus in the play named after him.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's tragic hero travels to Cyprus to defend it against the Turks.

definitions.meaning: continuing from 8-down, the newsman's paper is his publication or mouthpiece
a church instrument with many pipes has a great many notes

explanation.surface: A journalist's newspaper is well known.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening ellipsis continues 8-down, so 'his' is the newsman's.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper is the organ of a party or body, and the keyboard instrument produces many notes.

parts.note: the clue pictures an item such as a plate sold cheaply by a shop purely to draw customers in

explanation.definitionFit: A shop sells an item at a loss so as to attract customers who then buy other goods.

clue.text: It's to be used with breakdown of power

definitions.text: It's to be used with breakdown of power

indicators.note: a breakdown of a word breaks its letters apart so they can be reassembled

explanation.surface: Something to use when a car's engine fails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breakdown' looks like the car trouble of the surface and is; it also works as the signal to rearrange, so the whole clue doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope for hauling a vehicle is what you use when a car breaks down.

indicators.note: in places the student inside the college's name

parts.note: Eton College is a famous English public school
L stands for learner, a student

explanation.surface: A man called John is a pupil at a college.
explanation.walkthrough: Elton John is the singer; the definition is just his surname used as a pairing word.
explanation.definitionFit: The singer Elton John has the first name that goes with this John.

clue.text: Attacks of wind sometimes starting in the belly

indicators.note: in places the opening letter inside the word for the belly

parts.note: guts means the belly or abdomen

indicators.note: starting picks the first letter of the word sometimes

explanation.surface: Bouts of flatulence that sometimes begin in the stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusts are sudden blasts or attacks of wind.

indicators.note: turns says the word for a renegade is turned round

parts.note: a rat is a deserter or renegade

explanation.surface: A man named Jack becomes a traitor.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack and tar are both old words for a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are traditional slang for a sailor.

indicators.note: about says the word for anger goes round the other piece

parts.note: rage means anger
trad is short for traditional, long-established

explanation.surface: Fury over a traditional garment business.
explanation.definitionFit: The rag trade is an informal British term for the fashion and clothing business.

parts.note: ST is short for saint, a virtuous character

explanation.surface: Raising a glass to a good person.
explanation.definitionFit: To toast is to drink in honour of someone.

indicators.note: to gather something is to collect it in, so the workers surround the fruit

parts.note: worker ants are the classic crossword workers
a lime is a citrus fruit

explanation.surface: Labourers collect fruit to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Aliments are foods or nourishment.

clue.text: Unable to right wrong which is not clearly defined

indicators.note: wrong says the letters of unable are put in a wrong order

explanation.surface: Someone cannot put right an error that is vague.
explanation.definitionFit: Nebular means cloudy like a nebula, hence hazy and indistinct.

definitions.meaning: the ... horn is an alto clarinet, so the word can be called horned

explanation.definitionFit: The basset horn is an alto clarinet and the basset is a short-legged hunting dog.

definitions.meaning: a rare sense listed in Chambers: the continuous beat of a drum, like rat-a-tat
a climbing palm whose stems are used for cane furniture

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a climbing cane palm and, in Chambers, the rattle of a drum.

clue.text: It's not, they say, something of mine

definitions.text: It's not, they say, something of mine

parts.words: It's not, they say, something of mine
parts.note: the setter Gordius describes a thing of his own, followed by a word that sounds like a tangled tie, suggesting the famous impossible tangle cut by Alexander

explanation.walkthrough: The setter's pseudonym Gordius gives the adjective; 'not, they say' sounds like 'knot', the knot of Gordius that Alexander the Great cut.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means belonging to Gordius, the setter, and also names the famous knot.

clue.text: Rib on this bomb is going to be expensive

definitions.meaning: the anatomical Latin term for a rib

definitions.text: this bomb is going to be expensive
definitions.meaning: putting the word before bomb makes the phrase cost a bomb, British slang for very expensive

explanation.surface: Teasing about a bomb's price tag.
explanation.definitionFit: Costa is Latin for rib, and with a bomb added gives the British idiom for costing a lot.

parts.note: a concern is a business, abbreviated CO for company
the plural gives a second company abbreviation

explanation.surface: The worries a clown has.
explanation.walkthrough: Coco was a famous circus clown in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Coco the Clown was a celebrated circus clown, Nicolai Poliakoff.

clue.text: Guantanamo guards working to US terror model

parts.note: the Model T was Ford's famous car, so model gives T

indicators.note: working means the letters are put to work in a new order

explanation.surface: Guards at the Guantanamo camp follow an American pattern of terror.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link; 'working' rearranges US TERROR into ORTURERS, after T.
explanation.definitionFit: Guards accused of inflicting pain on detainees at Guantanamo are people who torture.

indicators.note: about says the bends go round the abbreviation for road

parts.note: two U-bends give two letters U

explanation.surface: Speech concerning curves in a highway.
explanation.definitionFit: Urdu is a language spoken in Pakistan and India.

definitions.meaning: a band of cloth worn round the waist
a ... is the sliding frame of a ... window

explanation.definitionFit: A sash is both a decorative waistband and the sliding frame of a window.

clue.text: It's about even and found in Ohio

parts.note: C is short for circa, about
level means even or flat

explanation.surface: Something roughly balanced turns up in an American state.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleveland is a major city in Ohio.

definitions.meaning: read as a noun sense, the fruit of the palm, sweet and sticky

explanation.definitionFit: Dates are both the sweet palm fruit and romantic meetings.
